svg.title: Storage-mode and capacity-sizing decisions for Fabric BI serving
svg.desc: Storage-mode selection (Import vs DirectQuery vs Direct Lake on OneLake), capacity memory-bound sizing, free-license viewer reach threshold (F64+), and operational implementation guardrails.
svg.text: Storage-Mode & Capacity-Sizing Decisions for Fabric BI Serving
Storage Mode Selection ➔ Capacity Memory Sizing ➔ F64 Licensing Threshold ➔ Operational Guardrails
STAGE 1: STORAGE MODE SELECTION FOR LAKEHOUSE-BACKED REPORTING

g.aria-label: Copy the data, or read it in place?
g.title: Storage-mode decision — Import, DirectQuery, and Direct Lake differ by whether data is copied and whether queries hit the source live.
Import — fast in-memory queries but stale between refreshes; the whole model must be memory-resident to answer queries.
DirectQuery — always fresh because every visual issues a live source query, but each render pays a round trip and is typically slower.
Direct Lake on OneLake — reads Delta columns straight from OneLake, pairing import-like speed with DirectQuery-like freshness and no copy or refresh job.
g.text: • Reads Delta Parquet straight from OneLake
• Zero data copy, zero scheduled refresh jobs
Skips SQL endpoint coupling; never falls back

g.aria-label: If one fact is huge: composite
g.title: Composite option — Direct Lake on OneLake supports composite models, so a very large fact stays Direct Lake while dimensions use Import or DirectQuery.

svg.text: STAGE 2: CAPACITY MEMORY BOUNDS & LICENSING REACH THRESHOLDS

g.aria-label: Resident columns fit under SKU memory?
g.title: Memory-fit decision — the SKU sets the per-model memory bound; estimate resident column footprint (VertiPaq DMVs) against it.
Fits — hot columns stay resident and queries run at import-like latency; size for sustained load, letting smoothing absorb spikes.
Over the bound — columns fall back to on-demand cold reads from OneLake at peak; step the SKU up, trim the model, or split workloads.
g.text: • Remedy: Step up F-SKU or trim model

g.title: Report-reach decision — F64+ lets free-license users view reports; below F64 every viewer needs a paid Pro/PPU seat.

g.aria-label: F64 as a licensing floor, not a load floor
g.title: F64 floor — broad viewer reach forces F64 or larger regardless of compute load, so licensing can set the SKU, not throughput.
Guardrails — write-side layout, mutation pattern, vacuum window, OneSecurity check, and the Block Public Internet Access go/no-go.
g.text: • V-Order & File Sizing: Write V-Ordered Delta with a ~1 GB Optimized Write target and low-cardinality partitions (<100–200 distinct)
• Append/Merge over Overwrite: Loading with Overwrite wipes commit history, forcing a full cold reload of all column segments
• Vacuum Retention Window: Keep vacuum retention strictly longer than framing cadence (e.g. 7+ days vs daily framing)
• Table File Count Ceiling: Keep individual Delta tables under 10,000 Parquet files (framing fails past this ceiling)
• Network Setting: Ensure tenant "Block Public Internet Access" is OFF; Direct Lake routes through public storage endpoints

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Diagram, August 2026. Sourced from Microsoft Fabric Direct Lake & Capacity Optimization.
